# NPL — National Physical Laboratory

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **Country** | United Kingdom |
| **City** | Teddington (London) |
| **Tier** | Core (Tier I) |
| **Primary ecosystem** | Metrology |
| **Relevant unit** | Thermal metrology — radiation thermometry and emissivity |

## Why it matters internationally

NPL is the United Kingdom's national metrology institute, and it anchors
emissivity in the **international comparison infrastructure**: NPL is a
documented participant in the **CCT Supplementary Comparison S1** of infrared
spectral normal emissivity (2–14 µm, 23–800 °C) alongside PTB, NIST, and
NMIJ. Comparisons of this kind are what make emissivity values measured in
different countries mutually trustworthy.

## Scope of activity

### Radiative properties measured

Infrared spectral normal emissivity · radiation thermometry · land-surface
temperature and emissivity.

### Capability envelope

- **CCT-S1 comparison scope:** spectral normal emissivity, 2–14 µm,
  23–800 °C.
- **Earth observation:** laboratory calibration and field measurement of
  land-surface temperature and emissivity, linking laboratory radiometry to
  satellite retrieval.

### Application domains

Non-contact thermometry · Earth observation and climate measurement ·
radiometric calibration and standards.
